healthcareSystem: Government-operated public healthcare system with one main hospital on each island. Healthcare is subsidized for citizens. Tourists pay out-of-pocket or through travel insurance.
qualityNotes: Basic healthcare available for common conditions. Joseph N. France General Hospital on St. Kitts is the primary facility. Limited specialist services — serious conditions require evacuation to Puerto Rico, Martinique, or the US. English-speaking staff throughout.
pharmacyHours: Mon-Fri 8am-6pm, Sat 8am-1pm. Limited Sunday/holiday availability. Look for 'Pharmacy'.
pharmacyTips: Several pharmacies in Basseterre stock common medications. Selection is more limited than in the US or Europe. Bring specialized medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Foreign prescriptions from licensed doctors are generally accepted at local pharmacies. Controlled substances require additional documentation. Bring extra supplies of any critical medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic painkillers
restrictedMeds.note: Opioid medications are strictly controlled. Carry original prescription and a doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Pseudoephedrine products
restrictedMeds.note: Products containing pseudoephedrine may be restricted. Carry documentation for cold medicines containing this ingredient.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring adequate supplies for your entire trip.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is strongly recommended. The islands have limited specialist care. Evacuation to Puerto Rico or the US mainland may be necessary for serious conditions.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry (unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country). Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Dengue fever and Zika virus are present — use insect repellent.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe to drink on both islands. Bottled water is widely available as an alternative.
foodSafetyTips: Food is generally safe at hotels and established restaurants. Be cautious with street food. Fresh seafood is excellent but ensure it is properly cooked. Be aware of ciguatera poisoning risk with certain reef fish.
medicalTourismNote: Not a medical tourism destination. The islands are primarily a tourist and cruise ship destination. Medical care is basic and focused on primary care and emergencies.
sources: St. Kitts and Nevis Ministry of Health
metaDescription: Health guide for Saint Kitts and Nevis. Emergency info, hospital details, pharmacy tips, travel insurance, and vaccination advice for travelers.

hospitals.name: Joseph N. France General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital on St. Kitts. Emergency department, general surgery, and basic specialist services. All staff speak English.

hospitals.name: Alexandra Hospital
hospitals.notes: Primary hospital on Nevis. Smaller facility with basic emergency and primary care. Serious cases transferred to St. Kitts or evacuated.

hospitals.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Several private dental practices in Basseterre. Limited on Nevis.
dentalCare.notes: Basic dental care is available. Private practices offer better quality than public clinics. Complex procedures may require travel off-island.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private dental clinics in Basseterre handle emergencies during business hours. After hours, contact the general hospital.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: 988 (US Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — may be accessible)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited — some counselors available through the public health system
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited but improving. Some counseling available through the Ministry of Health. English is the primary language.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Limited accessibility infrastructure. Tourism facilities are gradually improving accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Joseph N. France General Hospital has basic wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transportation. Taxis and private vehicles are the main transport options.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Major hotels and resorts are more likely to have accessible rooms. Historic sites and town streets may be difficult for wheelchair users. Cruise port area has some accessibility.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at Joseph N. France General Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: Follow standard hygiene practices. Healthcare capacity is limited.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals and clinics accept cash and major credit cards. Request itemized receipts and medical reports in English. File claims with your insurer upon return. Some facilities may assist with direct billing to major insurers.

commonCosts.note: US dollars widely accepted. Costs are moderate. Specialist care and complex procedures require evacuation, which significantly increases costs.

medicalEvacuation.note: Air ambulance evacuation is available from Robert L. Bradshaw International Airport. Travel time to Puerto Rico is approximately 1-2 hours by air. Ensure insurance covers Caribbean medical evacuation.

pharmacyChains.name: City Drug Store
pharmacyChains.identifier: Look for pharmacy signs in Basseterre

drugNameMap.note: Widely available. Both brand names commonly used.
